findings.text: replaces_document_relation settles a claim as contradicts whenever any relation form after a contrast also appears anywhere in the documentation, without checking the relation the claim actually asserts, so a document that describes its own design choice with the same construction vetoes itself; claim_settlement on "The calibration uses a linear relation instead of a quadratic one, and the linear coefficient is stated below." with that same text as the documentation returns "contradicts", and settled_claim_answers yields choice contradicts via document_relation_replaced on that code, which hard-vetoes an internally consistent document and is the over-refinement this node exists to remove; the amended 59/60 bar does not depend on this settlement.

the comment describes six samples and a former cutoff that fired on four, while supporting_evidence.matched_answers records ten samples and base_fires 7 and the test pins only two readings, so the source that pins the evidence states the wrong sample population.

the recall section points a reader at veto_replay.matched_answers, but the sampled answers are stored at supporting_evidence.matched_answers in srtj-docs-switch-causes.json and veto_replay has no such key, so the pointer resolves to nothing.

_names_a_position imports and calls imas_standard_names.parse inside the function on every invocation, with no cache, so score_documentation re-parses each name on each call and a catalog-wide lint sweep pays that parse per name per pass; the review package already imports the same library at audits.py:310, so the import belongs at module scope and the result belongs in a cache.
supporting_evidence.head_arm.revision is null and gate-delta.log names only the scratch tree paths, so the 71-versus-91 delta the manifest records cannot be tied to a revision by a later reader.
